Uzziel
ŭz'zĭ-ĕl
n. (youngest son of Kohath and uncle of Aaron — whose sons carried their cousins' bodies out of the camp after the strange fire)
From Hebrew 'Uzzi'el, “God is my strength”, from 'oz, strength, and 'El, God. The gentilic is Uzzielite. Several later Levites and one goldsmith of Nehemiah's wall bear the name.

Biblical Definition

Uzziel was the fourth and youngest son of Kohath — “and the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel” (Exo 6:18) — and so the uncle of Aaron and Moses. His own sons were “Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Zithri” (Exo 6:22), and two of them are called on at the most dreadful moment in the history of the priesthood. Nadab and Abihu had offered strange fire before the LORD and fire had gone out and devoured them; Aaron and his surviving sons were forbidden to mourn or to leave the sanctuary. So Moses sent for the cousins: “Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and said unto them, Come near, carry your brethren from before the sanctuary out of the camp” (Lev 10:4). They carried the bodies out in their coats. Elzaphan afterwards became chief of the whole Kohathite house (Num 3:30), set over the ark and the holy furniture. The Uzzielites number three hundred and twelve men in the wilderness census and appear again under David among the Levites David gathered to bring the ark up to Jerusalem the second and lawful time.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Uzziel; in sacred history he is the youngest son of Kohath and uncle of Aaron, father of the Uzzielite family of Levites.

expand to see more

UZZIEL, n. The son of Kohath and brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron; the name signifies God is my strength.

His sons were Mishael, Elzaphan and Zithri.

Mishael and Elzaphan carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp at the command of Moses.

Elzaphan was made chief of the families of the Kohathites.

The Uzzielites were numbered in the wilderness, and served in the house of the Lord in the days of David and Hezekiah.

Key Scripture

Exo 6:18 — "And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years."

Exo 6:22 — "And the sons of Uzziel; Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Zithri."

Lev 10:4 — "And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and said unto them, Come near, carry your brethren from before the sanctuary out of the camp."

Num 3:30 — "And the chief of the house of the father of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel."

Modern Corruption

The death of Nadab and Abihu is read as divine overreaction; Scripture presents it as the founding case for the regulative principle — worship God has not commanded is forbidden, however sincere.

expand to see more

Uzziel's sons carried out the bodies, so his family is bound to Leviticus 10, and that chapter is the hardest one in the Bible on the subject of worship. Nadab and Abihu offered incense with fire the LORD “commanded them not” (Lev 10:1). They were priests; the incense was real incense; the altar was the right altar; the God was the true God. The one defect was that this particular act had not been commanded. The modern objection — that God is unreasonably severe about a technicality — assumes worship is an offering of our sincerity, so that the form is incidental. Scripture assumes the opposite: worship is an approach to a holy God on terms He sets, and the terms are the mercy. This is the regulative principle the Reformed churches confess: what Scripture commands in worship is required, and what it has not commanded is not permitted.

The second thing in Lev 10 is the vocation given to Uzziel's sons, and it is a sober one. Somebody has to carry the bodies out. Aaron and his remaining sons could not; they were under oil and could not leave the door. So the cousins came near, took hold of coats, and did the worst job in Israel that day without a word recorded. There is a ministry of removing the wreckage after a judgment falls in a congregation — a discipline case, a fallen pastor, a scandal — and it is done by men who did not cause it and will get no credit for it. God names them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Uzzi'el (H5816), from 'oz (H5797), strength, and 'El (H410), God; 'esh zarah (H784 + H2114), strange fire.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Uzzi'el (H5816) — Uzziel, “God is my strength”; youngest son of Kohath.

Hebrew 'oz (H5797) — strength, might, boldness; the first element of the name.

Hebrew 'Eltsaphan (H469) — Elzaphan or Elizaphan, “God has hidden”; his son, made chief of the Kohathites.

Hebrew 'esh zarah — strange fire; fire the LORD “commanded them not” (Lev 10:1).

Hebrew tsawah (H6680) — to command, charge; the verb whose absence condemned Nadab and Abihu.

Usage

"“The sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel” — the four branches of the holiest house."

"“The sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron” — kinsmen called to a terrible errand."

"“Carry your brethren from before the sanctuary” — the office of clearing away a judgment."
